Problem_Classification.Domain: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) / Mesoscopic flow simulation
Problem_Classification.Algorithm: D2Q9 Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) with BGK (single-relaxation-time) collision and bounce-back boundaries
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Purpose: Simulates incompressible fluid flow on a 2D Cartesian lattice by evolving 9 discrete particle distribution functions per cell (1 rest + 4 axial + 4 diagonal). Each iteration produces an updated density rho and velocity u from the distributions, advancing toward the Navier–Stokes solution in the macroscopic limit.
Problem_Classification.Algorithm_Steps: 1. Buffer setup (host→device): copy initial distributions (if0, if1234, if5678), boundary mask (type), direction tables (dirX, dirY), and weights (w[9]) to device; duplicate into output buffers. 2. Time-step loop (host-side, `iterations` times): a. Launch `lbm` kernel with one thread per lattice cell. b. Per-thread inside kernel: i. Load this cell's 9 distributions (1 scalar + 2 double4) and its type flag. ii. Collide: - If boundary: bounce-back — swap opposite directions (1↔3, 2↔4, 5↔7, 6↔8). - If fluid: compute rho = Σf_i; compute u = (Σf_i·e_i)/rho for x,y; compute 9 equilibrium values f_eq via `ced` (1 + 3·eu + 4.5·eu² − 1.5·u²); blend f ← (1−ω)f + ω·f_eq. iii. Propagate (stream): for non-border cells, scatter each of the 8 non-rest post-collision values to the neighbor cell indicated by (dirX_i, dirY_i); write the rest population to the cell itself. c. Swap d_if{*} and d_of{*} pointers (double-buffering). 3. Copy final distributions device→host.
Problem_Classification.Reference_Complexity: Time: O(iterations × Nx × Ny) — constant work per cell per step Space: O(Nx × Ny) — two double-buffered copies of 9 distributions + 1 boundary mask

Bottleneck_Analysis.Classification: Memory-bound (with significant scatter-write penalty); borderline mixed against FP64 throughput.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Arithmetic_Intensity: Per fluid cell, minimum traffic = 9 doubles read (72 B) + 1 bool read (1 B) + 9 doubles written (72 B) ≈ 145 B (cache effects from neighbor reuse during scatter aside). FLOPs per fluid cell (approx., counting +,−,×,÷ each as 1): - rho reduction: 8 adds - u.x, u.y dot-products: 2 × (8 mul + 7 add) = 30, + 2 divisions ≈ 32 - 9 × ced: each ≈ 3 (u²) + 3 (eu) + 7 (polynomial) + 2 (rho·w·) ≈ 15 → 135 - BGK blend on 9 components: 9 × 3 ≈ 27 - Total ≈ 200–220 FLOP (FP64) Intensity ≈ 210 / 145 ≈ 1.45 FLOP/byte (FP64).
Bottleneck_Analysis.Ridge_Point_Comparison: RTX A6000 (GA102): FP64 peak ≈ 604 GFLOPS (FP64:FP32 = 1:64), bandwidth ≈ 768 GB/s ⇒ FP64 ridge ≈ 0.79 FLOP/byte. Intensity 1.45 sits ABOVE the FP64 ridge, suggesting nominally FP64-compute-bound. However, the propagation phase performs 8 scattered writes per thread to non-contiguous neighbor cells, halving (or worse) effective achievable bandwidth, which pulls the effective ridge upward and shifts the kernel back into memory-bound territory in practice.
Bottleneck_Analysis.Dominant_Limiter: DRAM/L2 traffic from uncoalesced scatter writes in the streaming step, compounded by warp divergence between fluid/boundary cells and by the FP64 division in u = Σ/rho. Secondary: low arithmetic intensity headroom against FP64 throughput on GA102's 1:64 FP64 unit.

Memory_Access_Profile.Pattern: Hybrid: streaming/coalesced reads of inputs at `pos`, but gather–scatter writes during propagation (each thread writes to 8 neighbor positions pos±1, pos±width, pos±width±1). Diagonal writes (s5–s8 → ±width±1) cross row boundaries and break full coalescing.
Memory_Access_Profile.Read_Write_Ratio: 1:1 by volume (9 doubles in, 9 doubles out per cell), plus 1 B boundary flag read.
Memory_Access_Profile.Reuse_Factor: Within one kernel launch: ~1 (each distribution loaded and stored exactly once per cell per step). Across iterations a value is touched 9 times (once per direction it streams along) but these are separated by a full kernel launch, so on-chip reuse is effectively zero without explicit shared-memory tiling.
Memory_Access_Profile.Coalescing_Feasibility: Reads: Natural — `pos = idx + width*idy` with idx running fastest gives coalesced 128-byte transactions for f0, f1234, f5678. Writes: Requires transformation — the scatter on 8 directions to neighbor cells produces partly coalesced (s0/s2 east/west), aligned-row (s1/s3 north/south), and unaligned diagonal (s4–s7) writes; a pull-scheme (read from neighbors, write to self) would convert these to coalesced stores.
Memory_Access_Profile.Optimal_Tiling_Hint: Switch to a "pull" streaming scheme so that all stores are to `pos` (coalesced) and only loads gather from neighbors (L1/L2 can absorb). For further speedup, tile (BX, BY) blocks into shared memory with halo (BX+2)·(BY+2): with BX=BY=32, halo tile = 34×34×9 doubles ≈ 73 KB — too large for one block on CC 8.6 (100 KB/SM but only one block fits). Drop to BX=32, BY=8 → 34×10×9 doubles ≈ 24 KB shared mem/block, easily fitting 2–3 concurrent blocks per SM. Alternatively, store only the eight non-rest populations needing neighbor access (~21 KB) and keep f0 in registers.

Parallelism_Structure.Granularity: One CUDA thread per lattice cell. Each thread performs a full collide + 1 self-write + up to 8 scatter writes.
Parallelism_Structure.Independence: Fully independent within a single kernel launch (uses double-buffered in/out arrays, no read-after-write across threads in the same step). Inter-iteration RAW dependency is resolved by the host-side pointer swap between launches.
Parallelism_Structure.Synchronization: None inside the kernel — no __syncthreads(), no atomics, no cooperative groups. Implicit global synchronization is provided by the kernel boundary between time steps.
Parallelism_Structure.Recommended_Block_Size: Current launch uses `grids(256,1)` as gridDim and `blocks(Nx/256, Ny)` as blockDim — this is unconventional and for typical Nx,Ny (e.g. 1024×1024) yields blockDim = (4,1024) = 4096 threads/block, exceeding the CC 8.6 hard limit of 1024 threads/block. Recommend a conventional 2D tiling such as 32×8 (256 threads) or 16×16 (256 threads): launching grid = (ceil(Nx/32), ceil(Ny/8)) gives natural memory coalescing along x and good occupancy. With ~64 regs/thread and modest shared-mem use, 256-thread blocks allow 4–6 concurrent blocks per SM (up to the 1536-thread-per-SM ceiling), which is the sweet spot for FP64-heavy stencil kernels on GA102.

Hardware_Constraints.Shared_Memory_Per_Block: 99 KB (101,376 B) opt-in maximum on CC 8.6; default 48 KB
Hardware_Constraints.GPU_Clock_Rate: 2100 MHz (max SM clock reported by nvidia-smi)

Data_Shape.Input_Dimensions: Nx = dims[0], Ny = dims[1] — runtime-supplied; not statically known from this source. Constraints implied by the launch arithmetic: Nx must be a multiple of GROUP_SIZE = 256, and Nx·Ny/256 ≤ 1024 (else blockDim exceeds device limit).
Data_Shape.Data_Type: Distributions: double (FP64). Boundary mask: bool (1 B). Direction tables (dirX/dirY): double8 passed by value. Weights: double[9]. Indices: 32-bit unsigned/int.
Data_Shape.Total_Memory_Footprint: Per cell: 2 × (1 + 4 + 4) doubles for double-buffered distributions + 1 bool = 2·9·8 + 1 = 145 B. Plus tiny constants: d_weight = 72 B; dirX, dirY passed by value through kernel args. Total device memory ≈ 145 · Nx · Ny B (e.g. ≈ 152 MB at 1024×1024, ≈ 608 MB at 2048×2048, ≈ 2.4 GB at 4096×4096), well within the 48 GB VRAM (≈10 GB free at probe time). Host mirror is similarly sized.
